summary: P1.11 legacy financial access hardening + P1.9 Excel import COMMIT cycle validated end-to-end against the live backend. 34/39 assertions passed. P1.11 fully validated: admin bypass, Julie scoped to acct only (403 on qc9434), Marc access to both, unassigned temp user 403 on all /acct/* and /qc9434/*. Financial smoke unchanged (all 9 endpoints 200 + non-empty). P1.9 preview OK (valid=1, errors=0), commit OK (created=1) with company id cmp_... and mandate mnd_... created; company appears in GET /api/companies, mandate is active with Julie as principal_user_id and Marc in collaborator_user_ids (verified directly in DB), logs contain mandate.created and company.bulk_imported. Two verification gaps and one cleanup gap detected (see issues). Baseline fully restored to clean state via targeted DB cleanup (companies=2, mandates=0, users=3, active company_access=3).

minor.issue: Not exposed (405/404). Admin cannot delete a company or mandate created by import via HTTP API — cleanup requires direct DB access. For a fiduciary workspace, an admin-only DELETE (or archive) endpoint would let ops undo an erroneous import.

Returned 200 but the user (temp-p111@accslegro.com) was NOT removed from the DB (still visible in GET /api/users afterwards). Either the endpoint is a soft-delete without hiding from the list, or the id shape passed did not match. Behaviour is inconsistent with a 200 response.

Returned an empty list even though DB clearly has the active row for Julie on the newly imported company. Endpoint appears to not return newly created access rows (missing join / stale filter). DB truth: Julie has active access on cmp_f893c... after commit.

mandate.created and company.bulk_imported events are present, but company.created event is NOT emitted during a fiduciary import commit. Expected all three per spec (company.created / mandate.created / company.bulk_imported).

action_items: Emit a company.created log event inside commit_company_import when a new company is created (currently only mandate.created and company.bulk_imported are logged).
Fix GET /api/users/{uid}/company-access — it returned [] for Julie post-import even though DB row exists (active=true) on the new company.
Investigate DELETE /api/users/{uid}: returned 200 but the user document was not removed (still listed in GET /api/users). Either hard-delete or ensure list endpoint filters soft-deleted users.
Consider adding admin-only DELETE endpoints for /api/companies/{id} and /api/mandates/{id} (currently 405) to allow undoing an erroneous fiduciary import via the API rather than direct DB.
No changes required in P1.11 access-control middleware or in financial formulas — both validated.
critical_code_review_comments: P1.11 middleware behaves correctly: admin bypass, unassigned user gets 403 on all legacy financial routes, per-company scoping (Julie 403 on qc9434) is enforced on both READ and WRITE (POST /qc9434/accounts).

Financial endpoints (acct dashboard/kpis/pnl-monthly/cashflow and qc9434 trial-balance/bilan/pnl/entries/invoices) all return 200 with non-empty payloads for 2026 — access-control refactor did not alter financial output.

commit_company_import correctly: creates the company (cmp_*), creates one active mandate (mnd_*) with the right principal/collaborator, and writes 2 active company_access rows (principal + collaborator) — verified directly in Mongo.
Logs pipeline emits mandate.created and company.bulk_imported but is missing company.created — inconsistent event coverage.

rca of the issue: The three non-blocking issues (missing company.created log, empty /users/{id}/company-access response, users DELETE returning 200 without removal) are independent of the P1.11 middleware change. The middleware itself and require_company_access enforcement are correct. Root cause of missing company.created log is that commit_company_import calls create_mandate_for_admin (which logs mandate.created) and emits company.bulk_imported at the batch level, but never emits a per-company company.created event — likely the log call was omitted when factoring the import flow.
